document.title: [Spec Decode] Enable adaptive DSpark on SM100 sparse MLA
document.body: ## Purpose Resolves #52785. This is part of the adaptive DSpark backend expansion tracked by #51303. Related GLM-5.2 DSpark bring-up context is in #50851. This enables adaptive DSpark verification with `FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMBackend`. It was validated end to end with `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` and `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark` on 4× NVIDIA B300. Before this change, startup failed for two independent reasons: 1. The sparse-MLA metadata builder derived token-to-request mappings from CPU query boundaries. Adaptive verification changes those boundaries on device without synchronizing them back to the CPU. 2. The target graph capability check included the draft model's FlashAttention backend. Draft attention is captured and capability-checked by its own graph manager, and it never consumes the target's adaptive query lengths. ## Changes - Add an SM100 FlashInfer sparse-MLA metadata builder that derives request IDs from device query boundaries and declares variable-length CUDA graph support. - Scope target CUDA graph and query-length compatibility checks to target attention layers while retaining draft groups needed by draft prefill. - Add a real B300 kernel regression using GLM-5.2 dimensions. It compares FlashInfer sparse MLA against SDPA with device query lengths `[1, 7, 3, 5]` and deliberately stale CPU lengths `[4, 4, 4, 4]`. - Add a unit regression proving draft-only groups are excluded without hiding mixed target/draft groups that still participate in target execution. ## Performance Scaled SPEED Bench qualitative sweep, 16K context, 512 output tokens, temperature 1.0, seed 0. The c1 run used 32 prompts, c16 used 128, and the remaining points used 256. Both configurations completed with zero failed requests. | Concurrency | Fixed k=7 tok/s | Adaptive tok/s | Gain | |---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 306.7 | 310.6 | +1.3% | | 16 | 2,084.4 | 2,093.5 | +0.4% | | 32 | 3,525.0 | 3,595.8 | +2.0% | | 64 | 5,236.8 | 5,538.8 | +5.8% | | 128 | 7,172.9 | 8,190.7 | +14.2% | | 256 | 7,720.4 | 10,316.8 | +33.6% | At c256, mean TPOT improved from 23.24 ms to 17.37 ms. A direct B300 kernel comparison also favored the selected FlashInfer SM100 backend over FlashMLA by 2.1–2.6× for uniform decode batches and 31.9× for a mixed 1/3/5/7-token adaptive shape. ## Model evaluation GSM8K, five-shot, 200 examples, greedy decoding, 2,048-token output limit: | Configuration | Accuracy | Invalid/truncated | |---|---:|---:| | Fixed k=7 | 89.0% | 1.0% | | Adaptive k≤7 | 91.0% | 0.5% | This shows no detected accuracy regression at this sample size; the two-point difference is not presented as statistically significant. HLE was also exercised, but 38/40 sampled outputs still truncated at an 8,192-token limit, so no HLE accuracy result is reported. ## Reproduction ```bash chg run -g=4 -- vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --load-format instanttensor \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --block-size 64 \ --max-model-len 16384 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --max-num-seqs 256 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \ --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size":2048}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-speculator.dspark","attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","enable_adaptive_verification":true}' ``` The full server completed target and draft CUDA graph capture and served the benchmark/evaluation requests successfully. ## Test plan ```bash chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py -q # 21 passed, 8 skipped .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py -q # 7 passed .venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-check --files .venv/bin/pre-commit run ruff-format --files .venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files # all passed ``` The focused CPU and B300 tests plus lint and mypy were rerun after rebasing onto current `main`. ## Not a duplicate Duplicate checks covered #51303 and adaptive DSpark/sparse-MLA keywords. #52362 enables adaptive verification on ROCm and changes AMD model/indexer paths; it does not overlap this CUDA SM100 metadata and target/draft graph-scoping change. #50694 addresses earlier FA3 and DSpark/DFlash proposer wiring for GLM-5.2. ## AI assistance AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used to investigate, implement, test, benchmark, and draft this change. The submitter reviewed every changed line, understands the change end to end, and ran the tests and model evaluations reported above.
